issues.title: v4: an optional key named after an Object.prototype member refuses an object that lacks it
issues.body:
An optional key whose name is an `Object.prototype` member (`constructor`, `toString`, `valueOf`, `hasOwnProperty`, `isPrototypeOf`, `propertyIsEnumerable`, `toLocaleString`) refuses a plain object that does not have it. Zod reads the inherited function as the key's value. For a schema that accepts anything, such as `z.unknown()`, it does the reverse: it accepts an object that lacks a required key, and copies the inherited function into the output.

**Versions:** zod 4.6.7, and the same in 4.0.0 and 3.25.76; Node 22.22.3.

```js
import * as z from "zod";

z.object({ constructor: z.string().optional() }).safeParse({});
z.object({ toString: z.string().exactOptional() }).safeParse(JSON.parse("{}"));
z.object({ valueOf: z.string().default("d") }).safeParse({});
z.object({ constructor: z.unknown() }).safeParse({});
```

| | expected | actual |
| - | - | - |
| 1 | `{ success: true, data: {} }` | `invalid_type` at `["constructor"]`: "Invalid input: expected string, received function" |
| 2 | `{ success: true, data: {} }` | the same, at `["toString"]` |
| 3 | `{ success: true, data: { valueOf: "d" } }` | the same, at `["valueOf"]`, and the default is not applied |
| 4 | failure: the key is required and absent | `{ success: true }`, and `data` has its own `constructor` property holding `Object` |

A control, `z.object({ name: z.string().optional() }).safeParse({})`, succeeds as expected.

It happens with `z.object`, `z.looseObject` and `z.strictObject`, with `.optional()`, `.exactOptional()` and `.default()`, on the JIT path and with `z.config({ jitless: true })`, and with `safeParseAsync`. Objects from `JSON.parse` and `Object.fromEntries(new URLSearchParams(...))` are plain objects, so any API with a field named, say, `constructor` refuses requests that leave it out.

**Cause:** presence is decided with `key in input` and the value is read as `input[key]`: in `handlePropertyResult` and the `$ZodObject` shape loop in `packages/zod/src/v4/core/schemas.ts`, and in the same two expressions in `$ZodObjectJIT`'s generated fast path. `in` and the property read both walk the prototype chain.

#6070 called the refusal of a *required* `toString` expected, which it is. For an optional key, or a default, it is not.

**Possible fix:** count a key as present unless it is only inherited from `Object.prototype`, and read an absent key as `undefined`. For example:

```js
key in input && (Object.hasOwn(input, key) || !(key in Object.prototype) || input[key] !== Object.prototype[key])
```

This keeps getters and other data inherited from a class prototype parsing as they do today. Patched locally into 4.6.7, it makes every case above behave as expected.

issues.title: z.cidrv6() accepts fractional prefix lengths (e.g. "2001:db8::/64.5")
issues.body:
`z.cidrv6()` accepts CIDRs whose prefix length is a decimal, which isn't a valid CIDR. `z.cidrv4()` rejects the same thing, and so does the JSON Schema pattern zod emits for `cidrv6`.

```ts
import { z } from "zod";

z.cidrv6().safeParse("2001:db8::/64.5").success; // true, expected false
z.cidrv6().safeParse("2001:db8::/0.5").success;  // true, expected false
z.cidrv4().safeParse("10.0.0.0/8.5").success;    // false

new RegExp(z.toJSONSchema(z.cidrv6()).pattern!).test("2001:db8::/64.5"); // false
```

Tested on zod 4.6.5 and on `main` (4.6.7).

`isValidCIDRv6` checks that the prefix round-trips through `Number()`, which catches leading zeros and `+`, but `"64.5"` round-trips fine, and there's no integer check. Adding `Number.isInteger(prefixNum)` to the range check fixes it. I have a fix with tests and can open a PR.

I found this by differential fuzzing zod's string validators against Node's built-ins (`net.isIPv4`/`isIPv6`) with fast-check, using Claude Code (claude-opus-5-5) to help write the harness and investigate.
issues.author: aahangan

comments.body:
PRs are currently limited to collaborators, so here's the fix on my fork in case it's useful:
https://github.com/colinhacks/zod/compare/main...aahangan:zod:fix-cidrv6-fractional-prefix

It adds `Number.isInteger(prefixNum)` to the existing range check in `isValidCIDRv6` and adds `/64.5` and `/0.5` cases to the CIDR v6 test (both fail without the fix). The full suite passes locally. Happy to open a PR once that's possible.

issues.title: Flatten nested unions in `toJSONSchema`
issues.body:
The current output is valid; this is about its shape. `z.toJSONSchema` already flattens most nesting: an intersection of intersections becomes one `allOf`, and `compactTypeUnion` turns a union of bare types, nested ones included, into a `type` array. A union whose options are anything more than a bare `type`, like objects, stays nested, though. Making it nullable, or putting it in another union, writes it as an `anyOf` inside an `anyOf`.

### Current output

```ts
import { z } from 'zod';

const Person = z.object({ name: z.string() });
const Company = z.object({ company: z.string() });
const Team = z.object({ team: z.string() });

console.log(JSON.stringify(z.toJSONSchema(z.union([Person, Company]).nullable())));
console.log(JSON.stringify(z.toJSONSchema(z.union([z.union([Person, Company]), Team]))));
```

Output (abridged):

```json
{"anyOf":[{"anyOf":[{…name…},{…company…}]},{"type":"null"}]}
{"anyOf":[{"anyOf":[{…name…},{…company…}]},{…team…}]}
```

The nested form means the same as the flat one, but it's harder to read in rendered docs, and client generators turn it into nested union types. The primitive version of the same schema, `z.union([z.string(), z.number()]).nullable()`, already comes out flat as `{"type":["string","number","null"]}`.

### Proposal

Write the flat form instead:

```json
{"anyOf":[{…name…},{…company…},{"type":"null"}]}
{"anyOf":[{…name…},{…company…},{…team…}]}
```

An `anyOf` option whose only keyword is `anyOf` can be replaced by its own options. An option carrying anything else, like a `description`, or one that `$defs` extraction turned into a `$ref`, stays as it is. `oneOf` can't be flattened this way: a value matching every option of `{ oneOf: [{ oneOf: [a, b] }, c] }` is accepted, while `{ oneOf: [a, b, c] }` rejects it.

### Where it would go

[`unionProcessor`](https://github.com/colinhacks/zod/blob/b500a2ee95134f81d74da7911d7378dd2853d042/packages/zod/src/v4/core/json-schema-processors.ts#L479-L494) and [`nullableProcessor`](https://github.com/colinhacks/zod/blob/b500a2ee95134f81d74da7911d7378dd2853d042/packages/zod/src/v4/core/json-schema-processors.ts#L719-L729) put each inner schema in as one option:

https://github.com/colinhacks/zod/blob/b500a2ee95134f81d74da7911d7378dd2853d042/packages/zod/src/v4/core/json-schema-processors.ts#L727

[`compactTypeUnion`](https://github.com/colinhacks/zod/blob/b500a2ee95134f81d74da7911d7378dd2853d042/packages/zod/src/v4/core/to-json-schema.ts#L443-L465), which `finalize` runs after `$ref`s are settled, folds a nested union only when every option is a bare `type`:

https://github.com/colinhacks/zod/blob/b500a2ee95134f81d74da7911d7378dd2853d042/packages/zod/src/v4/core/to-json-schema.ts#L452-L454

Splicing there, rather than in the processors, would leave a union that ends up behind a `$ref` alone, the same way `compactTypeUnion` does. The `intersectionProcessor` already splices a nested `allOf` the same way:

https://github.com/colinhacks/zod/blob/b500a2ee95134f81d74da7911d7378dd2853d042/packages/zod/src/v4/core/json-schema-processors.ts#L507-L512

### Related

The same nesting comes from other libraries' JSON Schema output, and from tools that convert it further:

- Effect-TS/effect#9533
- standard-community/standard-openapi#41
- open-circle/valibot#1710

### Version

`zod` 4.6.7
